justification: All requirements for Gift Aid on payment FP-0316-EL (Elaine Carter's £120 direct bank transfer on 16 March 2026) are satisfied. (1) The charity is HMRC-recognised as of 16 March 2026 [E02]. (2) The donation is from an individual [E06]. (3) Elaine has a signed Gift Aid declaration covering this payment [E05]. (4) The Gift Aid claimable on this donation (25p per £1, so £30 on £120) brings the total Gift Aid claimed for the year to £80, which does not exceed her £980 Income Tax paid for 2025–26, satisfying the tax-paid requirement [E04, E07]. (5) None of the exclusions apply: the payment was not made through Payroll Giving [E09], was not for goods or services [E10], involved no benefit to the donor [E11], was not a share transfer [E12], and was not from a charity card or CAF voucher [E13]. Therefore, the charity is eligible to claim Gift Aid on this donation.
scope_issues: The question is answered specifically for payment FP-0316-EL (Elaine Carter, £120, 16 March 2026). Other monthly direct debit payments and one-off donations from other donors would each need to be assessed individually against the same criteria, particularly the donor tax-paid requirement and Gift Aid declaration requirement.
